## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Cūḷahaṁsajātaka* (Ja 502) is a canonical Pali Jātaka story set at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana) [SuttaCentral]. According to its opening frame, the Buddha recounted this past-life narrative to the monastic community in response to their discussions regarding the venerable Ānanda's willingness to sacrifice his life, declaring that Ānanda had similarly renounced his life for him in past existences [SuttaCentral]. The central tale belongs to a widespread Buddhist cycle in which the Bodhisatta was born as a king of wild geese, who leads his flock from Mount Citrakūṭa to a lake near Benares and is captured in a fowler's snare [Brinker et al. 1996].
Scholars note that the narrative core of the wild goose tale has been preserved in multiple versions within the Pali canon, notably in Jātakas 502, 533, and 534 [Brinker et al. 1996]. The commentary to the Dhammasaṅgaṇī (*Atthasālinī*) cites a verse from a *Cūḷahaṁsajātaka* addressing the loyal goose commander Sumukha to illustrate lexical and chromatic distinctions of the term *hari* [Maung Tin 1921].
In terms of parallels and textual reuse, SuttaCentral records the *Mahāhaṁsajātaka* (Ja 534) as a curated passage-level parallel [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus confirms this shared textual tradition, identifying 7 shared passages with Ja 534 (longest §13.4–20.1) and 7 shared passages with the longer *Cūḷahaṁsajātaka* (Ja 533, longest §13.4–19.4) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus records extensive reuse within the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (parts 4 and 5) and detects alignments with the Tibetan *Jātakamālā* (D4150) [DharmaNexus].
